event.title: Artist Talk with Kerri Clarke: The Seven Sisters Possum-Skin Cloak
event.description:
Please join us for an artist talk and lively conversation between Indigenous Australian senior knowledge holder and artist Kerri Clarke (Boon Wurrung / Wemba Wemba) and Associate Professor of Anthropology Sabra Thorner. Their discussion will center on the making of the Seven Sisters Possum-Skin Cloak, currently on view in the Museum’s newly reinstalled galleries as part of MHCAM’s 150th anniversary celebration. Kerri was part of a team of four artists across three generations who visited campus in 2022 and made the cloak on-site, sharing their knowledge and stories with students and other members of the College community; it was the first time a possum-skin cloak was made on U.S. soil. The conversation will be followed by a Q & A with current students.

This virtual talk is free and open to the public; advance registration is required.

Kerri Clarke (Boon Wurrung / Wemba Wemba) works with communities across southeastern Australia, maintaining and establishing cultural connections for Aboriginal communities, families and young people. Kerri has participated in the revival and making of cultural objects for over 20 years, passing this knowledge onto family members and the next generations. In particular, she is an established Possum-Skin Cloak maker and has facilitated the creation and exhibition of many cloaks across the south east of Australia and internationally, including the Seven Sisters Possum-Skin Cloak in the permanent collection of the Mount Holyoke College Art Museum.

Co-sponsored by the MHC Anthropology Department, the Office of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, and the Mount Holyoke College Art Museum.

event.title: Mount Holyoke Symphony Orchestra: Mary Lyon Concert
event.description:
The Mount Holyoke Symphony Orchestra honors the pioneering spirit of its founder through music by two remarkable women separated by more than a century.

Elfrida Andrée's powerful Second Symphony, a landmark of nineteenth-century orchestral writing, is paired with Jennifer Higdon's luminous Blue Cathedral, a meditation on memory, hope, and transcendence that has become one of America's most beloved contemporary orchestral works.

  • Elfrida Andree - Symphony No. 2 in A Minor
  • Jennifer Higdon - Blue Cathedral

event.title: Writing Tía Eliana Back In: A Family Story of Exclusion and the Long Reach of Anti-Asian Racism in Peru
event.description:
This talk explores racism, exclusion, and the power of resistance in two parts.

The first part shares Alcalde’s journey to uncover and make visible the story of her great-aunt Eliana, whose family disowned her for marrying a Chinese man in 1940s Peru. The story offers an intimate look at how dominant national narratives and structures of belonging, gender, and racialization intersect with everyday lives, and of Eliana and her spouse, as told in her recent Spanish-language book on Eliana, family, and racism in Peru.

The second part draws on dozens of interviews during and after the pandemic to explore how Chinese-Peruvians continue to navigate and resist hypervisibility, racialization, and exclusion in contemporary Peru. The talk invites us to consider how challenging family silences and making visible forms of resistance can disrupt simplistic and exclusionary narratives of family, belonging, and nation.

Join virtually (requires registration): bit.ly/3VgGN2H

event.title: Memories and Reflections: A Native American Boarding School Survivor’s Story
event.description:
Ramona Klein, an enrolled member of the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa, will share her personal experiences as an Indian Boarding School survivor (1954-1958). During her talk she will discuss the lasting impact boarding schools have on Indigenous communities and its influence on her own life.

Ramona is an educator and President of Eagle Consulting, Inc. She has taught at kindergartens, post doctorate programs in the Bureau of Indian Affairs (Now BIE), public schools, private schools, tribal schools, colleges and universities. She has also served on many local, state, regional, national and international boards of directors.

Join virtually (requires registration): bit.ly/4BTRFUy
